en.title: Rockstar Cracks Down on GTA 6 Leaker, Channels Go Dark
en.summary: Rockstar Games has successfully taken down the channels used by a persistent GTA 6 leaker after a week of content spills. The publisher's swift action aims to regain control over sensitive pre-release information.
en.body:
After a relentless week of leaks that saw significant portions of **Grand Theft Auto VI** gameplay surface online, **Rockstar Games** has finally managed to shut down the primary channels used by the culprit. The leaker's dedicated website, which had become a hub for the stolen footage, now displays a "blocked ID" message, indicating it was taken down at **Rockstar's** request. Similarly, the leaker's Telegram channel has also been removed, with the service provider citing copyright infringement as the reason for the action.

This aggressive move comes after the leaks caused a significant ripple effect, reportedly leading to a nearly $3 billion drop in **Take-Two Interactive's** market valuation. The parent company of **Rockstar Games** has been actively pursuing the source, even issuing subpoena requests to tech giants like Microsoft and Discord in an effort to identify the individual responsible. While the leaker's main outlets are now offline, a clip showing **GTA 6's** loading screen and the leaker's PC briefly appeared on an X account, allegedly as proof they still possess a full build of the game. However, this account has since been removed, and the proliferation of fake accounts makes it difficult to ascertain the true status of the leaker.

## The Impact of Leaks on the Community

The **GTA 6** leaks have undeniably sent shockwaves through the gaming community. For months, fans have been meticulously dissecting every frame of the official trailers, theorizing about the setting of Vice City and the dual protagonists, Lucia and Jason. The unauthorized gameplay footage, while offering a tantalizing glimpse into the game's mechanics and atmosphere, has also overshadowed **Rockstar's** carefully crafted reveal strategy. Many fans expressed disappointment and frustration that the magic of discovery was diminished, while others were thrilled to see more of the game, regardless of the source. The debate continues about whether the leaks ultimately hurt or helped build anticipation, but the damage to **Rockstar's** control over its own narrative is evident.

## What's Next for GTA 6

With the primary leak channels neutralized, **Rockstar Games** will likely redouble its efforts to ensure no further unauthorized information is released. Fans can expect **Rockstar** to maintain its tight grip on future reveals, likely sticking to its planned content rollout. The official release date for **Grand Theft Auto VI** is still slated for 2025 on **PlayStation 5** and **Xbox Series X/S**, with no current plans announced for a PC version.

content_raw: Rockstar Games, after enduring a leaker’s relentless onslaught for about a week, has finally managed to take their official channels down. This includes the leaker’s Telegram channel as well as their website, which, as of this article, remains offline. This was first spotted by Polygon , which writes that the leaker’s site went down today, Aug. 22. The site, which we won’t provide here, currently returns a “blocked ID” message, saying it was blocked on request. “Requested content blocked by this node’s content policy,” the note on the site reads. Furthermore, it seems the Telegram channel used by the leaker is also down, with that service provider citing copyright infringement as the reason for the takedown. Image via Rockstar Games It is currently unknown if the leaker has any alternate modes of communication, though today a clip emerged on an X account claiming to be them, with a recording of GTA 6 ‘s loading screen and the leaker’s PC, supposed to serve as proof that they do, indeed, have a full build of the game. The account that first posted that seems to have been removed from X, though reuploads exist. Dozens of accounts carrying the same moniker as the leaker have appeared in the last week or so, so it’s hard to assume what’s real and what isn’t in a sea of fakers and copycats. Nevertheless, the leaks have caused tremendous damage to Rockstar and Take-Two Interactive. The latter, which owns Rockstar Games, lost nearly $3 billion in valuation as the leaks started dropping. The company has since issued subpoena requests for Microsoft and Discord, which should help it find the culprit.
